evidence: The MX-0812-SCL is an HDMI matrix switcher featuring 8 HDMI inputs and 12 outputs, each capable of handling 4K60 video, with advanced scaling for each output. It includes video processing capabilities for video walls, such as cropping and bezel correction, as well as multiview options like Picture-in-Picture and Quad view. Designed for various applications, it offers seamless switching, video wall control, and multiview support, alongside comprehensive audio support through HDMI de-embedding, analog, and Dante audio connections.

Featuring video wall processing capabilities, including cropping, bezel correction, scaling, and the ability to rotate images by 90, 180, or 270 degrees (Outputs 9-12). Additionally, it supports grouping functions for enhanced video wall presentations. The matrix also offers sophisticated multiview capabilities, supporting the simultaneous display of up to four separate video sources on a single screen. When activated, the multiview configuration is mirrored across HDMI outputs 1 to 4, ensuring consistent visual outputs on multiple displays. It supports a variety of multiview layouts, including Picture-in-Picture (PIP), Picture-by-Picture (PBP), Split Screen, Master view, and Quad view, catering to different viewing preferences and requirements. This flexibility makes it ideal for scenarios requiring real-time monitoring of multiple video feeds, such as control rooms, live events, and professional broadcasting environments.

The Matrix provides three distinct working modes tailored for system integrator projects: seamless matrix switching, video wall controller, and multiview switcher. This versatility makes it well-suited for a variety of applications and user needs. Designed with flexibility in mind, it supports both vertical and horizontal screen orientations and offers flexible configuration to meet the diverse requirements of professional environments.

The MX-0812-SCL integrates HDMI audio de-embedding, analog audio connections, and a Dante 4x4 network for expansive audio distribution. Specifically, the Matrix supports de-embedding audio from 8 HDMI inputs and includes 4 Dante inputs for extensive networked audio integration. Additionally, it provides 4 analog audio outputs and 4 Dante audio outputs, enabling flexible audio setups. A key highlight is the capability for independent audio switching, allowing any of the 12 audio inputs to be directed to any of the 8 audio outputs, ensuring tailored audio management for diverse requirements.

salesLanguage.headline: MX-0812-SCL: lets several sources feed several displays from one controlled system
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the customer has a known number of sources and displays and wants reliable routing without building a full networked AV system.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It keeps switching predictable and commercially efficient for fixed rooms or smaller multi-display systems.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Boardrooms, divisible rooms, education spaces, hospitality areas and fixed source-to-display systems.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Confirm the source and display count first. If those numbers are stable, a matrix may be the cleanest answer.
talkTrack: It avoids manual cable changes by routing sources to the right display.
It is often a strong commercial option where the system is fixed and not expected to grow heavily.
Scaling or seamless behaviour can help when displays and sources do not all match perfectly.
discoveryPrompts: How many sources need to be connected?
How many displays need independent control?
Are the display runs local HDMI, HDBaseT, or mixed?
Is future expansion likely, or is this a fixed room?
positioningNotes: For smaller fixed systems, check matrix before jumping to AV-over-IP.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not position as fully flexible site-wide routing if the customer needs scalable distributed AV.
